key_insight: RL2ML shows that finite-rollout reinforcement learning and maximum-likelihood-style training can be linked by a family of surrogate objectives with exactly unbiased gradients, so the right objective depends on rollout-level update geometry rather than just the population objective.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a principled way to choose and tune training objectives under a fixed rollout budget, improving stability and metric alignment in reward-based language-model training.
method: Defines a finite-rollout surrogate objective family spanning RL, ML-like, and beyond-ML regimes
Derives a closed-form, exactly unbiased gradient estimator for rollout-group updates
Introduces group-level update scale plus calibrated metric-gain and variance analysis to select the best surrogate
evidence_signal: The paper uses theoretical analysis of estimator-objective alignment, exact variance decomposition, and calibrated metric-gain reasoning under finite rollout groups rather than reporting a new benchmark dataset.
watch_item: The optimal surrogate is metric- and variance-dependent, so implementing it requires careful evaluation choice and variance estimation; the one-dimensional tuning problem still needs reliable calibration.
paper_title: RL2ML: Finite-Rollout Surrogate Objectives from Reinforcement Learning to Maximum Likelihood
